# DSR-0.2: Approved version 1 scope

Status: APPROVED (2026-09-30, America/Denver).

Decision owner: Operator. Approval recorded at 2026-10-01 04:16 UTC, after the operator selected reduced version 1 in this conversation: “reduced: approved, and needs to be recorded in the proper location”.

This is the authoritative scope decision for [DSR-0.2](../tickets/phase-0.md). It selects **Option R**, as defined in that ticket, not a hybrid. [DSR-0.3](../tickets/phase-0.md) applied it to the specification, plan, assumption tables and dependent tickets on 2026-10-01. Revision 6 remains the historical full design, not the approved build scope.

## Included and deferred behavior

Keep Bash as a claimed effect with one attempt and claim files; Write and Edit as repeatable effects with the existing special handling for an Edit whose new text contains its old text; the package hash, policy version and engine version checks; the lineage id; the workspace manifest and generation check; durable questions; and signed approvals and operator actions. Preserve tool policy enforcement, workspace confinement and the required real model proof. Approval of scope is not proof that these mechanisms work.

Any ambiguous Bash outcome parks the run and does not return a model facing `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` result. Ambiguity includes a timeout, Heartbeat Timeout, lost Worker, executor error after the claim, Schedule-To-Start timeout and any unclassified failure after start. The model cannot continue on an assumed Bash outcome.

Defer these five items from version 1:

- `redo`, including the `release_claim` recovery path.
- Keyed external service effects and the reserved `idempotency_key` field.
- The claims `high-water` counter and `expected_claim_ordinal`, including dependent reported counter fields.
- The additional `contract_version` integer.
- The model facing `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` result for Bash.

Claim files and stable effect identity remain. Dropping the claims counter does not drop the ordinal claim file by implication. The exact reset procedure remains the separate decision in DSR-0.8. A later expansion to Option F requires a new scope approval.

## G4 and S2 before and after

Before, G4 in revision 6 of the specification (historical quotation below; use [document locations](../canonical-documents.md) for the current specification):

“A retry of an Activity attempt or a Continue-As-New handover cannot repeat a completed keyed or repeatable effect. A keyed or claimed effect whose outcome is uncertain is reported to the model as unknown and is not repeated silently, absent an operator Activity command or a workspace reset, both of which the design detects and reports.”

After, approved scope wording for the rebaseline:

“A retry of an Activity attempt or a Continue-As-New handover must preserve the single application guarantees for the included Write and Edit effects. A claimed Bash effect whose outcome is uncertain parks the run without returning an unknown result to the model or authorizing another spawn. Claim guards, stable lineage and explicit reset handling remain required; keyed external service effects and `redo` are outside version 1.”

Before, S2 maps a lost Worker or an exhausted Bash attempt to `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and returns a tool error to the model. After, S2 parks the run with the uncertainty recorded for operator investigation. An existing claim prevents a second spawn; refusal remains a park cause, not a model invitation to repeat. Process survival on a partitioned host remains a residual risk, not a completed cancellation guarantee.

## Assumption disposition for the rebaseline

These are required scope dispositions, not new evidence statuses. Keep every assumption id. DSR-0.3 changes the owning tables and preserves the remaining proving work.

| Assumption | Disposition | Required scope treatment |
|---|---|---|
| A-04 | stays | Keep the Bash spawn guard; test uncertain outcomes as parks, not model facing unknown results. |
| A-05 | stays | Keep ordinal claims and divergent reset detection; narrow the response to refusal and park. |
| A-06 | stays | Keep lineage stability across reset and identity changes on Workflow Id reuse; remove keyed service guarantees. |
| A-07 | stays | Keep starter supplied lineage and the first Workflow Task reset test; remove keyed service wording. |
| A-08 | rewritten | Remove keyed outcomes and `redo`; ambiguous Bash, including Schedule-To-Start timeout, parks. |
| A-09 | stays | Preserve the special Edit single application guard and crash test. |
| A-10 | rewritten | Reduce the outcome mapping to the retained effect classes; do not let tool errors impersonate a safe pre claim failure. |
| A-11 | superseded | Keyed external service effects and their reserved argument are not offered in version 1. |
| A-13 | stays | Keep signed token binding, replay rejection and park identity; remove `redo` authority. |
| A-15 | stays | Keep handler ownership, inbound token enforcement and the scoped Pinned guarantee. |
| A-16 | rewritten | Keep rollout order and package, policy and engine checks; remove the additional contract version field and its tests. |
| A-21 | rewritten | Keep janitor safety, claim retention, manifest and generation checks; remove claims high water snapshot detection. Document the resulting mid run snapshot limitation. |
| A-23 | superseded | `redo` and its claim release or redispatch mechanism are deferred. |
| A-35 | stays | Contact and eventual upstream submission remain separate work; upstream acceptance is outside the PASS outcome. |
| A-36 | rewritten | Retain ownership of stable claimed effect identity for a later harness port, without a version 1 keyed service contract; remain outside PASS until Phase 7. |
| A-42 | stays | Continue-As-New wait age and cooldown are not removed by Option R. |
| A-45 | superseded | External service key retention is not needed when keyed effects are not offered. |
| A-47 | superseded | The keyed effect retry policy is outside version 1. |
| A-49 | stays | The options allowlist and runtime backstop proof remain required. |

All other assumptions stay in scope unless already excluded by the established PASS boundary. In particular, reducing recovery machinery does not retire the defer/resume, isolation or permission backstop assumptions.

## Affected tickets and checks

| Ticket | Required treatment in the rebaseline |
|---|---|
| DSR-0.3 | Apply this decision to both documents, manifests, assumption tables and ticket coverage. |
| DSR-0.8 | Keep reset detection and operator procedure; remove `redo` as a recovery choice. |
| DSR-0.10 | Candidate for SUPERSEDED: no version 1 keyed external service needs a key retention window. |
| DSR-2.1 | Keep workspace and claim identity preparation; remove claims high water state and contract version fields. |
| DSR-2.2 | Keep key and ordinal claim guards and one attempt; replace unknown result assertions with refusal and park checks. |
| DSR-2.3 | Rewrite mapping and fault tests for retained classes; remove keyed outcomes, claims high water and contract version cases. |
| DSR-2.4 | Keep repeatable Write and Edit checks, including the special Edit case. |
| DSR-2.5 | Candidate for SUPERSEDED: keyed author tools are deferred. |
| DSR-2.8 | Candidate for SUPERSEDED as a contract version feature; preserve package, policy and engine mismatch refusal checks in the retained executor work. |
| DSR-2.9 | Review only the approved Phase 2 scope and keep evidence for every retained guarantee. |
| DSR-3.1 | Keep handover and wait state; remove only fields belonging to dropped features. |
| DSR-3.2 | Keep signed token verification; remove authorization for `redo`. |
| DSR-3.3 | Retain park visibility and signed actions for supported causes; do not assume retry or checkpoint resume makes uncertain Bash safe. |
| DSR-3.5 | Keep lineage, reset and claim tests; replace model facing unknown assertions with park assertions. |
| DSR-3.7 | Exclude deferred redo work from the Phase 3 exit review; retain the reset and signed action checks. |
| DSR-3.8 | Candidate for SUPERSEDED: `redo` is deferred. |
| DSR-4.2 | Keep janitor and manifest generation checks; remove the claimed mid run snapshot detection guarantee provided only by the dropped counter. |

DSR-0.3 must reconcile later acceptance and review text with these changes. This decision lists supersession candidates; it does not mark unbuilt product work DONE or erase its assumption ids.

## Parked ambiguous Bash procedure

Open question, owner: Operator, recorded under DSR-0.8. Without `redo`, decide whether any signed `retry` or `resume_from_checkpoint` can safely resolve an ambiguous Bash park while claim files prevent a second spawn, or whether only `abort` is supported for that cause. The operational investigation procedure also needs to specify how an operator confirms an external outcome and handles a possibly surviving process.

This approval does not choose that procedure. Until it is settled and tested, park and expose the cause; do not authorize clearing claims, repeating Bash or resuming the model as if an outcome were known. This open question does not prevent recording the scope decision, but it still blocks the affected recovery implementation and its safety claim.

## PASS boundary and remaining authority

Use the existing [ticket index PASS boundary](../tickets/README.md): the outcome is the evidenced durable skill execution plugin, including real model proof. Upstream submission and the harness port are outside that outcome and remain Phase 7 work. A-35 and A-36 stay open for those excluded deliverables. The plan's pre M1 verification pass is replaced by Phase 1 real model evidence; final independent verification still applies in Phase 6.

No budget, credential, model selection, contact message, isolation level, gateway owner, deployment owner, lock repair, commit or push is approved by this scope decision. DSR-0.4 and DSR-0.5 remain the budget and contact gates.

## DSR-0.3 rebaseline completion evidence

Recorded on 2026-10-01, America/Denver. Three subagents updated the specification, plan and ticket bodies under separate file ownership. The lead reviewed the retained safety semantics and reran the checks below. This is documentation completion, not an independent design verdict or runtime proof.

- Specification evidence gate: PASS, 129 evidence records, 56 complete assumption rows, 46 local sources reopened, 81 sources validated structurally and zero resolution failures.
- Plan evidence gate with `--spec`: PASS, 89 evidence records, 56 matching assumption rows, 38 local sources reopened, 50 sources validated structurally and zero resolution failures.
- Canonical local ticket validator: PASS, 67 blocks, 58 work tickets and 9 containers. No relationship, phase gate or assumption coverage errors. Low confidence estimates remain disclosed, not approved by this result.
- Direct table comparison: identical assumption id sets and order, zero status differences and zero retirement milestone set differences. Every original A-01 through A-51 remains, with only A-52 through A-56 added. A-52 and A-55 are superseded scope provenance; A-53, A-54 and A-56 remain untested runtime obligations.
- Dropped feature search: `redo`, `release_claim`, claims `high-water`, `contract_version` and external `idempotency_key` occur only as superseded mechanisms or historical scope provenance in the specification and plan. Exceptional Edit retains its single attempt unknown result; model facing Bash uncertainty is superseded.
- Retained guarantees: key and ordinal claims, lineage, package/policy/engine checks, janitor retention, manifest generation, immediate M2 park or block, signed decisions and isolation requirements. Ambiguous Bash cannot drive another model segment. DSR-0.8 remains open; no safe recovery action was inferred. Mid run snapshot rollback and executor only version changes remain disclosed limits.

Moot ticket list applied under the approved scope: DSR-0.10, DSR-2.5, DSR-2.8 and DSR-3.8 are SUPERSEDED. Their ids, historical bodies and reciprocal links remain. DSR-2.3 now owns the retained mismatch checks formerly grouped with DSR-2.8. A-35 remains open for milestone M6 upstream submission, and A-36 for milestone M7 harness port; both are in ticket Phase 7 outside PASS.

Reproduce the checks from the workspace root:

```bash
python3 .claude/skills/spec-driven-temporal/scripts/evidence.py design/_private/historical-archive/spec.md design/_private/historical-archive/evidence.json
python3 .claude/skills/spec-driven-temporal/scripts/evidence.py design/_private/historical-archive/plan.md design/_private/historical-archive/plan-evidence.json --spec design/_private/historical-archive/spec.md
python3 .claude/skills/write-tickets/scripts/validate_local.py check design/_private/historical-archive/tickets
```

Structural URL validation does not prove remote contents or the design. Synthetic result injection, engine batching, option enforcement, exception wrapping, cancellation and interceptor replay still need their named proving work. No product code, paid call, contact, lock repair, commit or push was performed by this rebaseline.

Continuation on 2026-10-01 corrected stale scope statements in DSR-0.8, the DSR-1.1/1.2 progress paragraphs, and retained Phase 4/5 criteria. DSR-0.8 now records that a changed claim Run Id alone does not distinguish reset from Continue-As-New and cannot authorize safe recovery. The later tickets no longer treat retained Bash, approvals, handover or optional live output as an unresolved DSR-0.2 choice. Volume, isolation, budget and recovery decisions remain open. The lead reran both evidence gates and the canonical ticket validator after these corrections; all three still pass. A read only public issue check found no new reply and did not satisfy the contact gate.

## Offline implementation continuity approval

On 2026-10-01 the operator approved the proposed exception for code construction: “Proceed with the recommended continuity. \"May I start the offline harness and tool policy implementation now, with paid model calls disabled and contact deferred?\" Ok, i guess.”

DSR-1.1 and DSR-1.2 may start their offline implementation before DSR-0.4 and DSR-0.5 close. Keep those blocker links and record the limited exception in the active tickets. DSR-0.4 remains OPEN; DSR-0.5 remains IN PROGRESS with contact deferred. Neither is represented as satisfied. Do not send messages, invoke a paid provider, infer model or credential approval, or mark real model acceptance criteria complete. No commit or push is authorized.

The harness must fail closed before launching a real provider while authorization is absent. Default tests use deterministic local or mocked transports and require no provider credentials. Offline policy construction does not retire A-01/A-02 or prove engine interception; DSR-1.3 and the retained real model verification gates remain blocked. Phase 2 cannot start before DSR-1.9 closes on the required evidence. No other Phase 0 decision or scope exclusion is changed by this exception.
